theory.intro: A **primitive** of $f(x)$ is a function $F(x)$ whose derivative is $f(x)$, so $F'(x)=f(x)$. Finding a primitive reverses differentiation. Constants vanish when you differentiate, so every primitive of $f$ has the form $F(x)+C$.
facts: To test a candidate, differentiate it and check whether you get $f(x)$ back.
Any two primitives of the same function differ only by a constant.
The **general primitive** of $f(x)$ is $F(x)+C$, where $C$ is the **constant of integration**.
A function whose derivative is zero everywhere is a constant function.
If $F(x)$ is a primitive of $f(x)$, then $kF(x)$ is a primitive of $kf(x)$.
If $F(x)$ and $G(x)$ are primitives of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, then $F(x)+G(x)$ is a primitive of $f(x)+g(x)$.
The power rule for primitives, $\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}$, fails at $n=-1$ because dividing by $n+1$ would divide by zero.
steps: Expand brackets or write terms as powers of $x$ if needed
Find the primitive of each term: add 1 to the power, then divide by the new power
Combine the terms and add $+C$ for the general primitive

workedExamples.question_text: Find the general primitive function $f(x)$ given $f'(x)=12x^{5}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Increase the power by 1, divide by the new power and add $C$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{12x^{6}}{6}+C\\&=2x^{6}+C\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: Find the general primitive function $f(x)$ given $f'(x)=9x^{2}-6x+4$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Find the primitive of each term separately.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{9x^{3}}{3}-\frac{6x^{2}}{2}+4x+C\\&=3x^{3}-3x^{2}+4x+C\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A function $g(x)$ satisfies $g'(x)=0$ everywhere. Find its general primitive form.
workedExamples.solution_text:
A function whose derivative is zero everywhere is constant.
$g(x)=C$

workedExamples.question_text: Write $\frac{6}{x^{4}}$ using a negative power of $x$. Then find its general primitive, writing it as a fraction without a negative index.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\frac{6}{x^{4}}=6x^{-4}$
Increase the power to $-3$ and divide by $-3$.
$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\frac{6x^{-3}}{-3}+C\\&=-2x^{-3}+C\\&=-\frac{2}{x^{3}}+C\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: Find the general primitive of $(2x-3)(x+4)$ after expanding.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(2x-3)(x+4)\\&=2x^{2}+8x-3x-12\\&=2x^{2}+5x-12\end{align*}$
Find the primitive of each term.
$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\frac{2x^{3}}{3}+\frac{5x^{2}}{2}-12x+C\end{align*}$

A function $F(x)$ satisfies $F'(x)=0$ for every value of $x$.
What kind of function is $F(x)$?
foundation.solution_text:
$F'(x)=0$
Only a constant has a derivative of zero everywhere.
$F(x)=C$
